Responding vendors must demonstrate capability in backend system design, REST API development, structured data modeling, and technical integration. The scope includes: • Design and build of backend data layers across multiple ARIES modules (Design, Safety, Review). • Schema design, typed ORM data-access layers, and cross-module migrations. • Development and documentation of REST API endpoints supporting CRUD workflows (authorization pathway tracking, deliverable roadmaps, stakeholder/role features). • Integration adapters for external systems of record, including DOORS

This justification authorizes and dictates the acquisition of specific, brand-name industrial automation, network, and scanning hardware—specifically Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL) network switches, Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley control platforms, and Datalogic industrial scanners—necessary to support the deployment, integration, and sustainment of the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Material Flow System (MFS). The requirement for these specific manufacturers is based entirely on the technical parameters of the existing solution and the DLA Enterprise Approved Architecture, not on subjective vendor preference. Standardizing on these chosen enterprise brands is operationally necessary to align long-term sustainment, configuration management, and maintenance processes. The contractor shall provide services for a 40-hour formal training course over five (5) consecutive days for up to 12 students to facilitate the transition from film to non-film radiography. The training shall meet the requirements of NAS410 to Level 2 qualification. 5.2. Course Curriculum. The contractor shall provide a detailed course curriculum or topic outline prior to the award of a contract and when any changes are made. 5.3. Delivery of Training. The contractor shall provide required training at a facility to be determined prior to scheduled dates of performance. This may be at a contractor’s facility or an “on-site” government facility selected by the requiring activity. All students must attend the full course and pass a final examination (see 5.4) for course completion. Attendance shall be documented by the contractor. 5.4. Theory Training. The contractor shall deliver comprehensive theory training covering Computed Radiography (CR), Digital Radiography (DR), and Computed Tomography (CT). Training curriculum shall include, but not limited to, CR/DR/CT processes, equipment/components, techniques, image acquisition, data/image review, and relevant industry codes/specifications. 5.5. Practical Training. The contractor shall provide practical, hands-on training that includes, but not limited to, process controls for CR and DR. Image acquisition and/or CT is preferred but not required. 5.6. Examinations and Scoring. The contractor shall administer an examination to all attending students. The examination may be open-book from the contractor-provided training materials. Contractor shall be responsible for scoring the examinations and pass or fail decisions. 5.7.
